summary: A repository-owned pipeline turns implicit agent choreography into inspectable software. It is most defensible when every transition has typed artifacts, bounded authority, and executable acceptance conditions.

points.text: Roles should be defined by inputs, permitted tools, outputs, and stop conditions rather than persona prose. This makes a handoff testable and limits accidental authority inheritance.
Every branch and loop needs an explicit termination rule and budget. Multi-agent studies identify verification and termination failures even when roles appear reasonable.
Pipeline version, model and prompt versions, inputs, outputs, and transition decisions should be recorded together; otherwise a successful run cannot be reproduced or compared.
A pipeline should be selected only where task decomposition or independent verification adds measurable value. A graph is operational complexity, not evidence of better reasoning.
